source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (October reinforcements); R2226: narrative of the October fighting and Appendix E context
current_activity: landing and attached to the 1st Marine Division
notes: 164th Infantry (Americal) landed on 13 October 1942 and fought in the October defense of the Lunga perimeter under Vandegrift (Miller, ch. VI; Zimmerman’s October chapters). Confidence 0.7. Parent on this date is 1st Marine Division (attached); the regiment’s standing division is Americal.

location_qualifier: southern perimeter east of Bloody Ridge
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI, The Main Attacks; R2226: ch. VII, The Inland Phase, 24-26 October
current_activity: reinforcing the 7th Marines and holding through the second inland night
notes: Miller, ch. VI, and Zimmerman, ch. VII, agree that 3rd Battalion, 164th Infantry (Hall), marched from bivouac south of Henderson Field and entered Puller’s line between 0230 and 0330 on 25 October, that the two battalions were intermingled that night, and that on the night of 25–26 October the 16th and 29th Infantry attacked the 1st Battalion, 7th Marines, and 2nd and 3rd Battalions, 164th Infantry, including a strong attempt at the trail junction. Dated 25 October: the battalion’s first day in the line and the evening the second assault began. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: about 2,000 yards west of Point Cruz
source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Kokumbona Offensive, 1-4 November
current_activity: 1st Battalion advancing west of Point Cruz with the 2nd Marines
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry (Richards), was ordered forward from the Ilu on 3 November and on 4 November advanced with the 2nd Marines to about 2,000 yards west of Point Cruz. The rest of the regiment marched east toward Koli Point the same day (separate relocation claim). Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

current_activity: 2nd and 3rd Battalions marching east from the Ilu toward Koli Point
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: at 0600 on 4 November the 164th Infantry (less 1st Battalion, then west of Point Cruz) and B Company, 8th Marines, left the Ilu to march about seven miles toward a position south of the 7th Marines at Koli Point, with General Sebree accompanying. The regiment reached the Nalimbiu that afternoon and Koli Point on 6–7 November. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. A second 4 November claim (attack at Point Cruz) is a different action of the 1st Battalion the same day.

current_activity: 3rd Battalion reaching Koli Point, with 2nd Battalion following the next morning
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: on 5 November Rupertus ordered the 164th (less 1st Battalion) across the Nalimbiu and north to Koli Point. The 3rd Battalion reached Koli Point on the night of 6 November and was followed by the 2nd Battalion the next morning. Dated 6 November, the first day a battalion of the regiment reached Koli Point. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

current_activity: 2nd Battalion helping to clear the Gavaga Creek pocket
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: 2nd Battalion, 164th Infantry (less E Company at first), took position on 9 November on the right of 1st Battalion, 7th Marines, and on 11 November G Company closed a gap in the south. By the late afternoon of 11 November the battalion had pushed north to the beaches, and on 12 November the pocket was cleared. Headquarters, the antitank company, and 3rd Battalion had already been sent back to Lunga on 9 November. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.
